# Results — Study 599 (Tax-Loss Harvesting)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **systematic
tax-loss harvesting into a twin fund adds 0.3–1%/yr of after-tax alpha** — run as a daily-check,
**lot-level** TLH programme on SPY total-return with a wash-sale-safe SPY↔IVV twin swap, an
ST/LT rate grid, cohort analysis and a basis-lock-up decay curve. Pure **tax arithmetic** by
construction (the twin keeps market exposure identical), so the Signal is graded on the
mechanical after-tax delta the tape shows, with HAC/Welch inference where sampling noise exists.
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
As-of **2026-06-30** (last complete month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint
`cb2440086a51`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | SPY daily **total-return** closes (yfinance `auto_adjust=True`), 8,411 days, 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-30 (33.4 years) |
| Twin check | IVV vs SPY daily returns over 6,565 common days: corr **0.9932**, mean return gap **+0.01 bps/yr**, tracking-diff vol 223 bps/yr (timestamp jitter) — economically the same asset, so one price series carries both funds and the measured delta is pure tax timing |
| Engine | lot-level: every purchase (lump sum / $1k monthly contribution / harvest repurchase / reinvested tax saving) opens a lot; daily check, harvest when a lot is > **1%** below basis and ≥ **31 days** held (wash-sale-safe, two-twin routing); losses classified ST (< 366 d) / LT; tax saving reinvested same day; terminal liquidation pays per-lot CGT (both books) |
| Execution / costs | decision at close *t*, executed at close ***t*+1** (exactly one lag, skipped if the loss vanished overnight); **2 bps one-way × traded NAV** per leg (sell + rebuy + terminal); long-only, fully invested, no borrow |
| Assumptions (named) | harvested losses fully usable against gains taxed at the ST/LT pair (the $3,000 ordinary-income cap never binds — the 15/15 and 0/0 rows bracket it); SPY↔IVV treated as *not substantially identical* (industry practice, never formally IRS-blessed); no state taxes |
| Survivorship | none — a single continuously-listed index ETF, no panel selection |

## The lock-up punchline — a 1993 lump sum never harvests again

$100k invested 1993-02, run 33.4 years at 35/15: **0 harvests**, after-tax alpha **+0.0 bps/yr**.
SPY never revisits its 1993 basis after the first weeks — without fresh cash, the machine has
nothing to do for three decades.

## The rate grid — same market, same 667 harvests, different investor

Contributor ($10k + $1k/month, 1993-02 → 2026-06). Only the tax rates change between rows:

| rate pair (ST/LT) | after-tax alpha (bps/yr) | terminal after-tax uplift | harvests |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **35/15** (top bracket, ST offsets) | **+13.1** | +4.49% | 667 |
| 24/15 (middle bracket) | +8.8 | +3.00% | 667 |
| 15/15 (deferral only, no rate arb) | +5.4 | +1.82% | 667 |
| 35/15 **+ step-up at death** | **+13.9** | +4.75% | 667 |
| **0/0 (0% bracket — MYTH CHECK)** | **−0.4** | −0.13% | 667 |
| 0/0 + step-up (low-bracket donor) | −0.4 | −0.13% | 667 |

At 35/15 the programme harvests **$55,216** of losses (**88.5% short-term** — harvesting resets
the clock, so re-harvests are almost always ST), reinvests **$18,057** of tax savings, and repays
part of it at liquidation (terminal tax **$544,694** vs **$511,804** for buy-and-hold). The
**0/0 row is the arithmetic proof on the real tape**: with no tax rate the "alpha" is exactly
the trading costs (−0.4 bps/yr). Step-up turns deferral into forgiveness — but only for brackets
that deduct something (+13.9 vs +13.1; still −0.4 at 0/0).

## The Signal axis — 94 overlapping 10-year lump-sum cohorts (35/15)

One cohort per quarter-start (1993Q1 → 2016Q2), each a $100k lump sum run 10 years. Overlap =
39 quarters → Newey-West **lag 40** on the cohort mean.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| cohorts | 94 |
| **mean after-tax alpha** | **+46.0 bps/yr** |
| median | +23.5 bps/yr |
| sd / min / max | 53.9 / −0.4 / +189.0 |
| **HAC/NW t (lag 40)** | **+2.88** |
| share > 0 | 73.4% |
| **zero-harvest cohorts** | **24 of 94** |

Best cohort start **2007-10-01** (+189.0 bps/yr — it rides straight into 2008); worst
**2010-10-01** (−0.4 — costs plus an unlucky ST/LT flip). By start decade: 1990s +13.2,
2000s +90.8, 2010s +12.5 bps/yr. The mechanical delta **clears the desk's t ≥ 2 bar
on the real tape** — but the advertised 0.3–1%/yr band contains only the top-bracket *mean*
(0.46%); the **median cohort earns half the low end** (0.23%), and a quarter of cohorts earn
nothing at all.

## Path dependence — the harvest is a bear-market crop

Harvest yield (realised losses as % of average NAV) per calendar year, contributor run:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| richest years | 2008: 4.80%, 2002: 4.29%, 2009: 2.95%, 2001: 2.93%, 1994: 1.33%, 2003: 0.90% |
| bear years (2000-02, 2008-09, 2020, 2022) mean | **2.23%/yr** (n = 7) |
| calm years mean | 0.16%/yr (n = 27) |
| **Welch t (bear vs calm)** | **+2.72** (dof 6.1) |

Even 2020 (−34% in a month) and 2022 (−25% peak-to-trough) yield only ~0.1%: by then the
contributor's NAV is dominated by old, deeply-appreciated lots the drawdown never reaches.

## Decay — basis lock-up (average across the 94 ten-year cohorts)

Harvested loss as % of the initial stake, by year since inception:

| y1 | y2 | y3 | y4 | y5 | y6 | y7 | y8 | y9 | y10 |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **6.57%** | 3.19% | 2.58% | 1.81% | 1.60% | 0.46% | 0.19% | 0.15% | 0.15% | 0.17% |

Year-1 harvest **6.57%** of the stake; years 7–10 average **0.17%/yr** — a ~40× fade. The TLH
"alpha" is front-loaded by construction: it decays as the basis locks up.

## Robustness — the harvest threshold

10-year cohort sweep at 35/15, other trigger levels:

| harvest when loss > | cohort mean (bps/yr) | HAC t (lag 40) | harvests/cohort |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.5% | +45.7 | +2.94 | 4.3 |
| **1.0% (headline)** | **+46.0** | **+2.88** | 4.3 |
| 5.0% | +48.8 | +2.93 | 2.5 |

Flat in the trigger: with 2 bps legs and a 35% deduction, almost any loss is worth harvesting.

## Synthetic positive control — the volatility knob (machinery proof)

Deterministic GBM worlds, **20 seeds per cell** (mean ± sd across seeds; no single-seed
baselines). TLH alpha must rise with the planted volatility knob (volatility serves up the
harvestable drawdowns) and sit at ~zero minus costs when the rates are 0/0:

| planted σ | alpha at 35/15 (bps/yr) | sd across seeds | alpha at rates 0/0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.02 | +0.09 | 0.4 | −0.02 |
| 0.18 | +47.00 | 47.7 | −2.67 |
| 0.35 | +128.45 | 104.5 | −4.33 |

The engine detects exactly the effect it should and cannot manufacture value without a tax
rate. *(Machinery proof only — never cited in support of the Signal stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The mechanical after-tax delta shows on the tape: mean **+46.0 bps/yr**
  across 94 ten-year cohorts at 35/15 with **HAC t = +2.88** (lag 40), robust to the harvest
  threshold (t = 2.88–2.94) and the rate pair (t = 2.42–2.78); the bear-vs-calm harvest split
  carries Welch t = +2.72; the 0/0 run banks −0.4 bps/yr (pure costs), proving the delta is tax
  arithmetic, exactly as claimed. The advertised **0.3–1%/yr** holds only at the top bracket on
  the *mean* cohort — the median is +23.5 bps and the 33-year contributor nets +13.1.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** DIY costs are trivial (2 bps legs) and capacity unbounded, but the
  harvest is **front-loaded** (6.57% → 0.17%/yr as basis locks up), **path-dependent** (24/94
  cohorts harvest nothing; the crop is 2000–02/2008–09), requires external **short-term gains**
  to absorb losses at the headline 35%, and a typical 0.25%/yr robo fee exceeds the median
  cohort's 23.5 bps. Real, but decayed and regime-dependent — not INVESTABLE.
- **Who gets ZERO? — CONFIRMED.** The 0%-bracket retiree/donor banks **−0.4 bps/yr** (pure
  trading costs), with or without step-up at death; equal rates (15/15) keep only the +5.4
  bps/yr deferral value. The "alpha" is a **private tax-rate arbitrage** — it scales with the
  investor's marginal rates and is exactly nothing minus costs at rate zero.
